brief_title: Liraglutide Improve Cognitive Function in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
official_title: Liraglutide Improve Cognitive Function in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

interventions.name: Oral antidiabetic drugs: Metformin, Sulfonylureas (2nd generation), Thiazolidinediones, α-Glucosidase inhibitors, and Glinides

arm_groups.label: Placebo
intervention_names: Drug: Oral antidiabetic drugs: Metformin, Sulfonylureas (2nd generation), Thiazolidinediones, α-Glucosidase inhibitors, and Glinides

primary_outcomes.measure: Changes in cognitive function from baseline to 12 weeks

brief_summary: Patients with diabetes are susceptible to dementia, but regular therapy fails to reduce the risk of dementia. In previous observational study, the investigators found that liraglutide can improve cognitive function in patients with T2DM through a metabolism-independent pathway. Here the investigators aim to further verify such effects through a randomized, controlled study.

sites.facility: The third hospital affiliated to the Third Military Medical University

exclusion.text: other diseases affecting cognitive function (e.g., congenital dementia, brain trauma, epilepsy, severe hypoglycemic coma, cerebrovascular disease, ischemic heart disease, renal dysfunction);
alcohol abuse, mental illness, and psychoactive substance abuse;
any surgical or medical conditions that could significantly influence the absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion of interventional drugs;
